entries.title: Arachnus (the SR388 native)
entries.scope: Cover the original Arachnus (Japanese name Marukara), a rarely seen, armadillo-like SR388 native. In Metroid II and Metroid: Samus Returns it lies curled in an orb atop an Area 2 Chozo Statue, posing as an Item Sphere after taking the Spring Ball. In Metroid II only Bombs hurt it. In Samus Returns it attacks with rolling charges, ramming and fireballs, and is weak to Missiles; sources call it optional there, so verify. Defeating it gives Samus the Spring Ball. End with a single line noting that the X later copied it on the BSL. This entry fixes the dangling 'See also: Arachnus' in Creatures: Fauna of SR388 and Creatures: Fauna of the BSL station. Do NOT repeat: Arachnus-X on the BSL Main Deck and the Morph Ball it returned (X Parasite: X-mimicked creatures of the BSL, part 1); Chozo Statue and Item Sphere mechanics, including its line on Arachnus (Chozo: Chozo Statues, Item Spheres and Torizo); the Area 2 description (SR388: Areas of SR388); Spring Ball mechanics (Equipment: Morph Ball and Spring Ball).

entries.title: Deorem, the Acid Worm, Kiru Giru and Imago (lesser guardians of the first Zebes mission)
entries.scope: Cover the lesser guardians of Metroid: Zero Mission. Deorem: a spiked Brinstar worm that ambushes from the ceiling. Only its open eye is vulnerable, to Missiles. It gives the Charge Beam if beaten quickly; otherwise it flees and must be fought again. The Acid Worm (titled 'Mua' on Metroid Wiki): it attacks from the acid pit of Kraid's area while Samus crosses on handholds, and the acid drains once it dies. The Kiru Giru larva: the creature she had to get around on the way to the Wave Beam. Imago: its adult form, with a stinger weak point, tied to the Super Missiles. Sources disagree on where the larva is, so use the Metroid Wiki pages rather than walkthrough summaries and leave out unconfirmed locations. Do NOT repeat: Kraid and Mini Kraid (Zebes: Kraid); Ridley, Mecha Ridley, Mother Brain and the Ruins Test (their own entries); the mission narrative (Zebes: Samus's first Zebes mission (Zero Mission)); Charge Beam, Wave Beam and Super Missile mechanics or the acquisition lines already in those Equipment entries.

entries.title: Goyagma and Vorash (Pyrosphere bosses of the Bottle Ship)
entries.scope: Vorash: a lava-dwelling monster of Sector 3 (Pyrosphere) that kept trying to swallow Samus. It had swallowed a Grapple Point; a charged Ice Beam shot exposes it, she drags Vorash ashore with the Grapple Beam, and the lava level drops after it dies. Goyagma: a lava-controlling monster of Sector 3, fought right as Adam authorized the Varia Suit, after Samus had crossed the Pyrosphere without it. It grabs her and she breaks free with a charged shot; she then freezes its arm with the Ice Beam and Overblasts its head. Note neutrally that the Varia timing is one of Other M's most discussed moments. Do NOT repeat: the authorization reasoning (Universe: Why Samus loses her abilities; Equipment: Varia Suit); the Pyrosphere description (Other M: The Bottle Ship); the incident narrative (Other M: The Bottle Ship incident); other Bottle Ship fauna (Creatures: Fauna of the Bottle Ship); Overblast mechanics (new Other M combat techniques entry).

entries.title: Incinerator Drone and Hive Mecha (Chozo drones of the Chozo Ruins)
entries.scope: Incinerator Drone: a Chozo high-temperature waste-disposal drone in the Burn Dome of Tallon IV's Chozo Ruins (Metroid Prime). It rouses a Barbed War Wasp hive, and destroying it gave Samus the Morph Ball Bomb. Hive Mecha: a second-generation Chozo security drone in the Hive Totem that works with Ram War Wasps, guards the Missile Launcher and is harmed only by the Power Beam. Add a release caveat: per sources it appears only in some releases (the original NTSC version) and not in later ones. Verify this; if you cannot, say only that it is absent from some versions. Frame both as Chozo machinery still running long after the Chozo withdrew. Do NOT repeat: the Chozo Ruins description (Prime: Regions of Tallon IV); War Wasps (Creatures: Fauna of Tallon IV); Bomb and Missile mechanics (Equipment entries); Chozo technology in general (Chozo: Chozo technology and legacy); Flaahgra (Prime: Flaahgra, Thardus and the Omega Pirate). Do not cover the Plated Beetle; it is already in Fauna of Tallon IV, and its key is handled as a KEYS line.

entries.title: Samus's reputation: how troopers, Pirates, hunters and the Federation see her
entries.scope: A synthesis entry to guide NPC reactions to Samus. (a) Galactic Federation leadership: it trusts her with contracts it cannot handle itself (Dane, Aurora Units), yet programs she exposed regard her warily (Fusion defiance, in one clause). (b) Marines and troopers: awe and admiration, e.g. Nora Armstrong idolizes her 'famously unshakable demeanor'. The 07th Platoon received her coolly; only Anthony was friendly. (c) Space Pirates: they fear 'the Hunter' as a priority target. Give one sentence, with a pointer, since the Pirate records live elsewhere. (d) Fellow bounty hunters: a mix of respect and rivalry. Rundas, Ghor and Gandrayda worked beside her. Gandrayda vowed to bring 'Aran's bloody helmet' to Dark Samus; verify the quote. The Prime Hunters were rivals, and Sylux hates her. (e) Prophecy titles from the Chozo, Luminoth and Lamorn ('Chosen One'): one sentence. (f) The wider galaxy: she is 'the most famous hunter of her time', and strangers react with legend and rumor, which contrasts with her taciturn reality. Quote canon lines with attribution. Do NOT repeat: her own personality (Samus: Personality and temperament); her views of other people (Samus: How she regards Adam, Anthony, Ridley, Dark Samus and Sylux); Pirate logs (Space Pirates: The Pirates and Samus (the Hunter)); bounty-hunting mechanics (Technology: Bounty hunting in the Metroid galaxy; Galactic Federation: Bounty hunters and the Federation); hunter biographies. KEYS: use only multi-word phrases (e.g. 'your reputation', 'her reputation', 'heard of you', 'living legend', 'legendary hunter'); never bare 'reputation', 'famous', 'fame' or 'hero'.

entries.title: Humans and Earth
entries.scope: Short entry of about 250-300 words. Humanity is the species Samus was born into and the backbone of the Galactic Federation's military, research and colonies (the Marines, Adam Malkovich, Anthony Higgs, Madeline Bergman, Myles MacKenzie). Earth is humanity's homeworld: its mythology names Federation ships (Olympus, Valhalla, Tyr), and per the manga Samus's birthplace, K-2L, was an Earth colony. Samus is human by birth, but her Chozo and Metroid DNA set her apart; give that one sentence and point to the DNA entry. Answer 'are you human?' only at that level. Source from the Metroid Wiki Earth and Human pages. An earlier fact-check removed 'Earth hosts the Federation HQ' as unsourced, so make no claim about where the HQ is beyond what Galactic Federation: Daiban and Federation Headquarters says. Do NOT repeat: K-2L details (Samus: K-2L (Samus's home colony)); DNA details (Samus: Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become); Federation structure (Galactic Federation (overview)); the Humans bullet in Technology: Species of the galaxy (index). Do not use bare 'human' as a key: it would fire on nearly every message. KEYS: make this entry selective. Primary keys may include 'Earth', 'humans', 'humanity', 'human race', 'Earthling', but put 3-8 Metroid-context words in secondary_keys (e.g. 'Federation', 'colony', 'Chozo', 'K-2L', 'species', 'galaxy') with selective_logic AND_ANY, so ordinary chat about people or the planet does not fire it.

entries.title: Exotic materials: Cordite, Bendezium, Denzium, Talloric Alloy, Brinstone, Radion and Urithic Ore
entries.scope: Short glossary entry of about 250-300 words on the dense or exotic substances that Samus's weapons are rated against: which weapon breaks which (Cordite: Super Missiles; Bendezium: Power Bombs, Prime era; Denzium: Power Bombs, Aether; Talloric Alloy: Bombs; Brinstone and Radion: Missiles), where she met each, and what the scan data says about its composition or origin, per the Metroid Wiki pages. Also cover Urithic Ore, the Zebes crust mineral suited to underground construction. Gives in-character answers to 'what is Cordite?'. Do NOT repeat: Phazite (Phazon entries); afloraltite (Samus: K-2L (Samus's home colony)); Fuel Gel (Federation and Norion entries); weapon mechanics beyond one clause each (Equipment: Missiles and Super Missiles; Equipment: Bombs, Power Bombs and Cross Bombs); the Zebes planet description (Zebes: Zebes (planet overview)).
